note: One step per surface of the consumer inventory. The tracked-tree rename is not a step here: it runs first (python -m scripts.rename apply) and this sequence covers everything the rename cannot reach by itself. Steps are ordered; each names what it changes, the check that proves it, and how it is undone.

checkout_directory.statement: The checkout directory does not move at cutover. The repository and the import package are renamed in place, and the directory that holds them keeps its name and its absolute path, because the worktree root, every worktree's .env and .venv links, and the editable install all resolve through it. Every step that names the checkout (C0, C2, C5, C7) means this same directory. If the sequence ever needs it to move, that is its own step with its own check and its own undo, run after those consumers have been re-pointed.

tracked_rename.evidence_split: Under docs/evidence everything keeps its bytes except *.py and *.sh, which are renamed like any other code. The kept list states that as an exclusion on the path, not as a list of kept extensions, so a new evidence file type is kept without a change to the list; the same split is made for docs/figures. The kept list is the authority for the split and this sequence only names it.

steps.title: Freeze writers and record the at-rest evidence
steps.step: Record `git worktree list --porcelain`, `squeue -u $USER -h -o '%i|%j|%T|%M|%N'`, `scontrol show job` for each job, `systemctl --user list-units --all 'imas-codex*' 'reckon-watch-imas-codex*'` and the live pointer listing under `~/.config/reckon/crew/live/` filtered on project imas-codex. Resolve or carry every worktree that holds unmerged commits: list it, and for each either merge its commits or park them on a named branch before any path moves. Do not touch a retained worktree's files. Stop writers: no graph writer, no scheduler job using the shared environment, the graph stopped for C5/C7. Then list every session's queued and awaiting-upstream requests for the project, group them by the session that owns them, and have each owner drop its own before C1; read the `queued_requests` block in this step for the listing command, the instruction to give each owner, and when a re-dispatch is safe.

queued_requests.listing: Read every pointer file under `~/.config/reckon/crew/live/*.json` whose top-level `project` is `imas-codex`, and list its `run_id`, `phase` and owning `session`. Take the requests whose phase is `queued` or `awaiting-upstream` (a `held` request names its `prior_phase`, and is treated as the phase it names) and group them by owner session. The listing is not the project's retained history: `~/.config/reckon/crew/run_store.db` holds that and it does not move.
queued_requests.operator_instruction: The operator runs the listing in this step, then hands each owner the run ids listed for its session and instructs it to drop those requests before C1 starts. Each owner confirms the drop with the run ids it cleared, and the operator records that confirmation beside the listing. After C2's check has passed, the operator instructs the same owners to re-dispatch the dropped nodes. No owner needs a new project key: reckon keeps the key it has, so the re-dispatch targets the same project it came from.
queued_requests.rule: Each owner drops its own queued and awaiting-upstream requests for the project before the tracked rename (C1) and re-dispatches them after C2's check passes. A queued request stores a base revision before the rename and write paths under the old package name, so one admitted after C1 would build a pre-rename tree on top of the renamed one. Re-dispatch is safe once C2 has rebuilt and verified the shared environment under the new distribution name, because a re-dispatched node then runs the renamed tool against the renamed tree; reckon's project key does not change, so no request has to be re-registered under a different project. Nobody else drops anyone's requests: the freeze lists them and each owner clears its own.
queued_requests.parked_worktree: A retained worktree may be recorded as parked by its owner under a kept ref; it is then not carried across the cutover, and C7 re-attaches or drains it only if its owner later unparks it.

steps.check: Every retained worktree appears in the recorded list with a disposition (merged, carried, or abandoned with its commit sha named); the live pointer listing prints for project imas-codex and names every queued and awaiting-upstream request with its owner session; each owner's drop of its own requests is recorded with the run ids it dropped, so an empty queued list is a recorded fact rather than a search that saw nothing; the scheduler listing shows no job whose working directory or command is the shared environment. The recorded list is committed with the cutover landing record.
steps.undo: Nothing was changed: the step only records. Removing the freeze is restarting the writers, which each later step's check re-admits.

steps.title: Apply the repeatable rename to the primary branch
steps.step: On the primary branch at the quiet window, from the repository root: `python -m scripts.rename apply`, then `python -m scripts.rename check` (exit 0) and commit. The tracked change carries the distribution name, the import package, the [tool.iter-codex] settings table, the IMAS_CODEX->ITER_CODEX environment prefix, the root path constants the code resolves, unit and container names as tracked files declare them, and both tracked MCP client files (.mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json: key iter-cx, project path and command renamed).
steps.check: `python -m scripts.rename check` exits 0 and reports every old-name hit under a kept path; `python -m scripts.rename cutover` reports zero unaccounted surfaces; a second `apply` reports zero changed files; `git grep -n imas_codex -- <each kept path from scripts/rename/kept_names.json>` returns only kept entries, and every file under `docs/evidence` is kept by default except the Python and shell beside it, which are renamed, so a new evidence file type needed no list change and a bare ':!docs/evidence' would hide exactly the files this check must see. NOTE: use `git grep` on the kept list, never a bare prefix replacement, so imas_standard_names and imas-dd are not casualties.; every dotted identifier that appears in a kept path (`<old name>.<artifact>`, a stored schema or receipt identity) is unchanged in the code that reads it
steps.undo: `git revert` the single rename commit on the primary branch; the tree returns byte-identically because the tool only rewrites text and moves paths it names in its report.

steps.title: Rebuild the shared environment under the new distribution name
steps.step: In the main checkout after C1: `uv sync --extra test` (the extra cannot be a default; without it the suite aborts at collection). The sync regenerates the console scripts (11 declared entry points, now iter-codex etc.), the 175 venv bin wrappers that embed the checkout path, and the generated models. Migrate the untracked `.env` in the same checkout: the settings prefix moves with the code, so every key the settings table composes from it must be renamed too (the measured example is `OPENROUTER_API_KEY_IMAS_CODEX` to `OPENROUTER_API_KEY_ITER_CODEX`; values are copied, never printed), and the same applies to any private YAML under the config root that names an environment variable. Reinstall the user-bin wrapper `~/.local/bin/plan` and edit the three matching ~/.bashrc lines (22, 23, 160) that name the checkout or the command.
steps.check: `uv pip show iter-codex` reports the new distribution and editable path; `command -v iter-codex` resolves inside the environment; `iter-codex --version` (or the CLI's revision report) prints the cutover commit; `rg -l imas_codex /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-codex/.venv/bin | wc -l` falls to the third-party wrappers only (activation files are regenerated, and the editable .pth now names iter_codex).; every settings-derived variable the code now reads resolves in `.env`, proven by the LLM-dependent default-tier tests that failed without it
steps.undo: Check out the pre-rename commit in the main checkout and run the same sync, or restore the environment from the recorded pre-cutover `uv pip freeze`; the environment is a build artifact and no tracked file is involved.; restore the saved `.env` copy

steps.title: Install the renamed user units and launch scripts
steps.step: Install `iter-codex-embed.service`, `iter-codex-graph-push.service`, `iter-codex-graph-push.timer`, `iter-codex-llm.service` and `reckon-watch-iter-codex.service` beside the old units, install the six launch scripts under `~/.local/share/iter-codex/services/` (codex-embed.sh, codex-neo4j.sh, embed.sh, llm-launcher.sh, llm.sh, neo4j.sh), re-point the two enablement links, `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, `disable` the old units, then `enable --now` the new timer. The scheduler job names themselves (`codex-neo4j`, `codex-embed`) carry no project name and stay: their command and working directory move to the new share root, which is what the inventory matched on.
steps.check: `systemctl --user list-units 'iter-codex*' 'reckon-watch-iter-codex*'` shows the timer active/waiting and no old unit loaded or enabled; `ls ~/.config/systemd/user/*.wants` names the new units; `squeue-style` listing (`squeue -u $USER -h -o '%i|%j|%T|%M|%N'`) shows codex-neo4j and codex-embed running with `~/.local/share/iter-codex/services/...` commands, and the graph client discovers the service from inside a SLURM step as well as on a login node.
steps.undo: `systemctl --user disable --now the new timer`, remove the new unit files and wants links, re-enable the old units (their files are retained until this step's check passes), and move the launch scripts back with the root move of C4 reversed.

steps.title: Move the live state, cache and config roots and migrate stored credentials
steps.step: With the graph and embedding services stopped: `mv ~/.local/share/imas-codex ~/.local/share/iter-codex`, `mv ~/.config/imas-codex ~/.config/iter-codex`, `mv ~/.cache/imas-codex ~/.cache/iter-codex`. The retained cache entries (51) are historical reports and checkouts: move them with the root, do not rewrite their bytes. Copy each keyring entry `imas-codex/<service>` to `iter-codex/<service>` (`keyring get`/`keyring set` per service, never printing the value) and leave the old entries until C8's zero-consumer check; the private gist id in the config root and the graph manifest move with the root.
steps.check: The new CLI resolves all three roots (`iter-codex config paths` or the equivalent reports ~/.config/iter-codex, ~/.local/share/iter-codex, ~/.cache/iter-codex); the graph manifest is found at the new location and its pushed_to image identity is unchanged; credentials resolve for a read-only probe first, then `iter-codex graph status` succeeds against the running service.
steps.undo: Stop the services, `mv` each root back, restore the keyring reads to the old service names (the old entries were kept), and restart under the old units.

steps.title: Re-point the external MCP clients
steps.step: In `~/.codex/config.toml` replace the `imas-cx` server key with `iter-cx`, its project path with the same checkout directory (which does not move at cutover, see `checkout_directory`) and its command with `iter-codex`. In `~/.claude.json` keep both `imas-dd` definitions unchanged and replace only a full-server `imas-cx` definition if one is present. Both tracked files (.mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json) already moved in C1. Take a copy of each external file before editing.
steps.check: Each client's own listing (e.g. `codex mcp list`) shows `iter-cx` and `imas-dd`; a reconnected client lists the full server's tools; the DD-only definition still resolves to the same endpoint. `rg --hidden 'imas-cx' ~/.codex/config.toml ~/.claude.json` returns nothing.
steps.undo: Restore the copied files and reconnect; server and client are independent, so no server state changed.

steps.title: Migrate the two stored graph templates and keep the error evidence
steps.step: Query the two `DataAccess.connection_template` values that embed `from imas_codex.remote.executor import run_python_script` (exact node ids in the inventory receipt) and rewrite only the import module to `iter_codex.remote.executor`, after reading the current value into the cutover receipt. Do not touch the six FacilityPath checkout descriptions or the two ancestor listings: they describe a discovery provenance at the observed path, and the checkout directory does not move at cutover (`checkout_directory`), so the descriptions stay true; re-discover rather than rewrite them if a later step ever moves it. Leave the 17 `CHECKED_WITH.error` values alone.
steps.check: A bounded read (`MATCH (d:DataAccess) WHERE d.connection_template CONTAINS 'imas_codex' RETURN count(d)`) returns 0, and the same query for `iter_codex` returns the same two nodes; `MATCH (n)-[r:CHECKED_WITH]->() WHERE r.error CONTAINS 'imas-codex' RETURN count(r)` still returns 17. The templates execute on a bounded trial read from a compute node.
steps.undo: Write the two captured pre-cutover template strings back by node id; the error evidence was never changed.

steps.title: Check that reckon still serves the project under its existing key
steps.step: Nothing is moved or rewritten. Reckon's project key, its mounts entry, the state directory docs/state/imas-codex, its stored reviews, its ledger rows and the worktree root keep their names and their bytes. Reckon has no supported way to rename a project key, so the key stays. A value that differs from C0's listing is a failure of an earlier step: report it, never repair it by moving the key or the directory.
steps.check: Reckon lists the project under imas-codex with its retained run count equal to the count C0 recorded; one plan review and one run review open by their stored ids; one plan resolves by slug; the rename check still exits 0 with docs/state and docs/.reckon reported as kept.
steps.undo: Nothing changed: there is nothing to undo.

unchanged.mounts_entry: The project's entry in the reckon mounts file, unchanged.
unchanged.state_directory: docs/state/imas-codex, its name and its bytes, unchanged.
unchanged.stored_reviews: Every stored plan and run review, unchanged and resolvable by id.
unchanged.ledger_rows: The project's retained ledger rows, including the 1109 counted.
unchanged.worktree_root: The worktree root and its worktrees, unchanged.
unchanged.rule: None of these is rewritten; a difference is reported, not repaired.

steps.out_of_scope: Migrating the key or the state directory to a new name is a later change, made only when reckon supports renaming a key without new plan and run identities.

steps.title: Rename the two repositories and publish the images under the new name
steps.step: Rename the fork `Simon-McIntosh/imas-codex` and, once the organisation's agreement is recorded, `iterorganization/imas-codex` to `iter-codex`; update both remotes and the badges and URLs the tracked files carry. GitHub redirects the old address, but container packages do not move: publish `iter-codex-graph`, `iter-codex-graph-*` and the application image under the new owner names and keep every published old tag. Build the separate Azure image as `iterorganization/iter-codex` and confirm the workflow derives the GHCR name from the repository. Node briefs on the primary branch: those under docs/evidence keep their .html, .json and .md bytes, and the Python beside them is renamed with the rest of the code by C1; a re-dispatched brief is regenerated by its owner from the current template, which C1 renamed.
steps.check: `git remote -v` shows the new URLs; `gh repo view` resolves both; `docker pull ghcr.io/<owner>/iter-codex-graph:<tag>` succeeds and the graph manifest records the new image; the old package identities still list their published tags; the Azure count is re-measured with `az` present or recorded as still not measured, never as zero.
steps.undo: Rename the repositories back (redirects follow), restore the remotes, and leave the new images in place: neither rename destroys old package identities or tags.

steps.title: Regenerate a gate script still in use; keep the rest as evidence
steps.step: `~/.cache/imas-codex-live-rewrite/` keeps its name and its bytes. Landed run records cite it by absolute path, so it is evidence of those runs, not a product surface: nothing rewrites, copies over, moves or deletes it, and no step renames it to `~/.cache/iter-codex-live-rewrite/`. Record its file listing and a per-file digest as the step's receipt. A script whose owning session still needs it live is regenerated by that owner, from the current brief and the current tool, in a new directory the owner names; the record says per file whether it was kept as evidence or regenerated, and where the regenerated copy lives.

kept_directory.citation: Landed run records cite this directory by absolute path, so its name and bytes are the record of those runs.
kept_directory.regenerated_by: the owning session, in a new directory it names and records; a regenerated script is a new file, never an edit of the kept one.
kept_directory.rule: Nothing rewrites, moves, copies over or deletes this directory.

steps.check: `find ~/.cache/imas-codex-live-rewrite -type f` and its digest listing equal the pre-step receipt exactly, so every kept script is still at its cited path with its cited bytes; each script an owner still needs live is recorded with its regenerated path under a new directory and that path exists; `rg -l 'imas[-_]codex' ~/.cache/iter-codex-live-rewrite` is never run, because this step creates no such directory and a copy under the new name would be a rewrite of the evidence.
steps.undo: Nothing outside the new regeneration directories changed; removing a regenerated script returns the owner to the kept one at its cited path.

steps.title: Re-run the inventory and close the transition
steps.step: Re-run the inventory collectors named in docs/evidence/fragments/codac-uda-signals/current-name-consumer-inventory.html against the live system and compare row by row: each row must be renamed (count now zero or naming the new identity), kept (the IMAS surfaces with their count unchanged, and reckon's project key with docs/state/imas-codex under that key), migrated (the value now names the new root, key or template), or still recorded as not measured. No new live reference to the old name may remain outside the kept list. Only then remove the §10 transition alias, if the earlier stage created one; this rehearsal's rename ships no old console script, so the alias removal is a no-op unless the transition stage installed it.
steps.check: The row-by-row comparison has zero unaccounted surfaces and zero rows still naming the old name in a renamed surface; the two kept DD client keys, the standard-names distribution and import, and the IMAS dependencies are present; `python -m scripts.rename check` and `python -m scripts.rename cutover` both exit 0 on the merged tree.
steps.undo: This step only reads and compares. A row that disagrees sends the operator back to the step that owns it with that step's undo.
